citation: Lindstrom R, Lindholm P, Kallijarvi J, Palgi M, Saarma M, Heino TI. Exploring the Conserved Role of MANF in the Unfolded Protein Response in Drosophila melanogaster. PLoS One. 2016. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0151550.
description: This paper documents MANF as a conserved regulator of the unfolded protein response and reports genetic interactions between Drosophila Manf and homologs of GRP78, PERK, and XBP1. It supports interpreting Hspa5/Hyou1/Pdia6-like induction after Manf perturbation as a MANF-UPR response rather than as generic transcriptional drift.

citation: Koppinen TK, Reyes CR, Nam J, Singh A, Mandal S, Beckett L, Montedeoca A, Kallionpaa TAE, Lindahl M, Rivera FJ, Voutilainen MH. Modulation of the unfolded protein response with a C-terminal fragment of MANF facilitates recovery in models of multiple sclerosis. Molecular Therapy. 2025. doi:10.1016/j.ymthe.2025.10.023.
description: This CNS demyelination study shows that MANF-derived treatment suppresses chronic activation of all three UPR branches in oligodendroglia and that MANF-deficient brains respond poorly after demyelination. It supplies the target-specific expectation that reducing MANF function can increase UPR-marker expression.

citation: Shiga Y, Rangel Olguin AG, El Hajji S, Belforte N, Quintero H, Dotigny F, Alarcon-Martinez L, Krishnaswamy A, Di Polo A. Endoplasmic reticulum stress-related deficits in calcium clearance promote neuronal dysfunction that is prevented by SERCA2 gene augmentation. Cell Reports Medicine. 2024. doi:10.1016/j.xcrm.2024.101839.
description: This paper links loss of neuronal SERCA2/ATP2A2 expression to impaired calcium clearance and ER stress, and shows that SERCA2 augmentation lowers ER stress in injured retinal neurons. It predicts that Atp2a2 loss should elevate ER-stress and integrated-stress transcripts.

citation: Wang M, Ye R, Barron E, Baumeister P, Mao C, Luo S, Fu Y, Luo B, Dubeau L, Hinton DR, Lee AS. Essential role of the unfolded protein response regulator GRP78/BiP in protection from neuronal apoptosis. Cell Death and Differentiation. 2009. doi:10.1038/cdd.2009.144.
description: Purkinje-cell GRP78/BiP depletion activates the UPR and induces GRP94, PDI, CHOP, and GADD34. Because Hspa5 encodes GRP78/BiP, the paper directly supports increased UPR gene expression after Hspa5 loss in neurons.

citation: Katoh M, Katoh M. WNT signaling pathway and stem cell signaling network. Clinical Cancer Research. 2007. doi:10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-06-2316.
description: This review summarizes the canonical Wnt cascade, placing LRP5/LRP6 upstream as Wnt coreceptors and APC as a beta-catenin destruction-complex inhibitor, with Axin2 and other genes as beta-catenin/TCF outputs. It supports opposite directional expectations for Apc loss and Lrp6 loss on Wnt target transcripts.

citation: Peterson TR, Sengupta SS, Harris TE, Carmack AE, Kang SA, Balderas E, Guertin DA, Madden KL, Carpenter AE, Finck BN, Sabatini DM. mTOR complex 1 regulates lipin 1 localization to control the SREBP pathway. Cell. 2011. doi:10.1016/j.cell.2011.06.034.
description: This work establishes mTORC1 as an upstream activator of SREBP-dependent lipogenic and sterolgenic transcription. Since TSC1 inhibits mTORC1, it supplies the mechanistic chain by which Tsc1 loss predicts increased SREBP target expression.

citation: Malek N, Mrowczynska E, Michrowska A, Mazurkiewicz E, Pavlyk I, Mazur AJ. Knockout of ACTB and ACTG1 with CRISPR/Cas9(D10A) Technique Shows that Non-Muscle beta and gamma Actin Are Not Equal in Relation to Human Melanoma Cells Motility and Focal Adhesion Formation. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2020. doi:10.3390/ijms21082746.
description: ACTB knockout in human melanoma cells is compensated by increased ACTG1 expression and alters focal-adhesion and actin-cytoskeleton behavior. It provides a target-specific but non-neuronal bridge for ACTB loss to an actin-remodeling response.

citation: Chen J, Fuhler NA, Noguchi KK, Dougherty JD. MYT1L is required for suppressing earlier neuronal development programs in the adult mouse brain. Genome Research. 2023. doi:10.1101/gr.277413.122.
description: Adult mouse cortical MYT1L loss derepresses earlier neuronal-development programs through chromatin changes and SIN3B/HDAC2-associated repression. The paper supports a specific but incomplete bridge from Myt1l loss to developmental-state transcription in neurons.

citation: Chen H, LaFlamme CW, Wang YD, Blan AW, Koehler N, Mendonca Moraes R, Olszewski AR, Almanza Fuerte EP, Bonkowski ES, Bajpai R, Lavado A, Pruett-Miller SM, Mefford HC. Patient-derived models of UBA5-associated encephalopathy identify defects in neurodevelopment and highlight potential therapeutic avenues. Science Translational Medicine. 2025. doi:10.1126/scitranslmed.adn8417.
description: Patient UBA5 variants in cortical organoids and engineered cells perturb UFMylation, ER homeostasis, and the unfolded protein response. It supports an indirect UBA5-to-proteostasis bridge but does not identify the exact mitochondrial and H1f4-heavy modules observed here.

citation: Karouzaki S, Peta C, Tsirimonaki E, Mangoura D. PKCepsilon-dependent H-Ras activation encompasses the recruitment of the RasGEF SOS1 and of the RasGAP neurofibromin in the lipid rafts of embryonic neurons. Neurochemistry International. 2019. doi:10.1016/j.neuint.2019.104582.
description: This study places neurofibromin, the Nf1 gene product, in neuronal lipid rafts as a RasGAP that terminates H-Ras signaling. It provides the target-specific Ras/ERK bridge used to interpret activity-gene induction after Nf1 perturbation.
